Summary: This bill would require the Department for the Aging (DFTA), in consultation with the Cabinet for Older New Yorkers, to develop an informational toolkit about programs, benefits, and services available to New Yorkers aged 60 and up. The toolkit must include materials containing information about rent freeze programs; information about meal delivery programs; information about other public and non-public programs, benefits, and services for older adults; contact information for DFTA; and contact information for other relevant agencies and organizations. DFTA would have to distribute a printed version of the toolkit at older adult centers, to homebound older adults, and to new participants in DFTA programs. DFTA would also have to post the toolkit on its website and ensure that the printed and digital versions are accessible. This bill would require regular updates to the toolkit.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to an informational toolkit on available programs, benefits, and services for older adults

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Chapter 2 of title 21 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 21-220 to read as follows: 
§ 21-220 Informational toolkit for older adults. a. Development and content. The commissioner, in consultation with the cabinet for older New Yorkers established pursuant to section 2405 of the charter, shall develop an informational toolkit to educate the public about programs, benefits, and services available to older adults that are provided or administered by an agency or a service provider contracted by an agency. Such toolkit shall include:
1. Any materials made available by the department pursuant to sections 11-139, 21-211, 21-214, 21-215, 21-216, and 21-217;
2. Any other materials produced by the department to educate older adults about public programs, benefits, and services available to older adults;
3. Contact information for the department; and
4. Contact information for other agencies and service providers contracted by agencies that  provide a program, benefit, or service available to older adults that a member of the public may contact to obtain additional information regarding such programs, benefits, or services.
b. Distribution of toolkit. 1. No later than July 1, 2027, the commissioner shall require each older adult center to distribute a printed version of such toolkit to older adults entering such older adult center and post signage in a conspicuous location informing older adults that these materials are available. The commissioner shall also distribute a printed version of such toolkit to homebound older adults. 
2. Each year, the commissioner shall identify individuals who are newly enrolled participants in a program, benefit, or service administered by the department and distribute a printed version of such toolkit to such individuals. 
3. No later than July 1, 2027, the commissioner shall make a digital version of the toolkit available on the department’s website and provide a clear and conspicuous link on such website to request a printed version of such toolkit.
c. Accessibility. The materials contained in such toolkit shall be made available in English and each of the designated citywide languages as defined in section 23-1101, and, as necessary, shall incorporate accessibility features including the use of clear and accessible language, the use of large print, legible fonts, instructive graphics, and braille. 
d. Updates. The commissioner shall update both the printed and the digital version of the toolkit required by this section within 45 days after the department makes a substantive update to any of the materials referenced in paragraphs 1 or 2 of subdivision a of this section. The commissioner shall review any other materials included in the printed and digital versions of such toolkit on an annual basis and update such materials as the commissioner deems appropriate.
§ 2. This local law takes effect immediately.
